bull.b: Rapid growth in core product revenue indicates improving adoption of Sequans’ cellular IoT silicon beyond one-time licensing activity. This supports a more durable revenue base, while increasing production volumes can strengthen customer relationships and improve operating leverage over time.

Conversion of design wins into mass production provides tangible evidence that customers are deploying Sequans technology at scale. The production pipeline and backlog extending into 2027 create multi-period revenue visibility and support the company’s longer-term growth strategy.

Exiting cryptocurrency holdings and redeeming convertible debt simplify the capital structure and reduce exposure to non-core asset volatility. A cleaner balance sheet should let management focus financial resources on scaling semiconductor products and funding strategic technology development.

bear.b: Severe TTM losses show that current revenue levels do not yet cover the company’s operating cost base. Until product scaling produces sustained operating leverage, Sequans may need continued balance-sheet resources or external financing to support operations and growth.

The shift toward lower-margin product revenue has materially reduced gross profitability, making the path to breakeven more dependent on volume growth and cost control. Persistent margin pressure could limit cash generation even if design wins continue converting into shipments.

The NYSE deficiency creates an ongoing corporate and execution burden over the coming months. Sequans must demonstrate a credible recovery plan within the cure process, and failure to restore compliance could disrupt its listing status and complicate access to investors.
